reason: The provided sources fully support a surprising 45-second story with 12 substantiated claims meeting the criteria.
story: Launched in 2018, NASA's Parker Solar Probe became the fastest human-made object in history, plunging directly through the blistering outer atmosphere of the Sun, known as the corona. Designed to endure extreme solar radiation, the spacecraft utilizes a massive 4.5-inch-thick carbon-composite heat shield that can withstand temperatures reaching roughly 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit, while keeping its sensitive instruments at a cool 85 degrees. By executing seven Venus gravity assists over a seven-year span to shrink its orbit, the probe reached a blistering heliocentric speed of approximately 430,000 miles per hour at its closest approach. This historic mission finally allows scientists to directly sample solar wind and solve decades-old mysteries regarding why the Sun's corona is vastly hotter than its actual surface.
angle: Plunging through the Sun's atmosphere at a record-shattering 430,000 miles per hour while protected by a carbon shield, the Parker Solar Probe is the fastest human-made craft ever built.

claims.claim: The Parker Solar Probe was launched by NASA in 2018.
The project honors physicist Eugene Newman Parker.
It is the first NASA spacecraft named after a living person.
The mission features seven Venus gravity assists over seven years.
The spacecraft completes 24 total orbits around the Sun.
At closest approach, it reaches speeds of approximately 430,000 mph (690,000 km/h to 700,000 kph).
The heat shield is approximately 4.5 inches thick and made of carbon-composite material.
The heat shield can withstand temperatures reaching nearly 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit (1,370 to 1,377 °C).
The shield maintains internal instrument temperatures at around 29 to 30 degrees Celsius (85 degrees Fahrenheit).
It is the first spacecraft to fly into the low solar corona and touch the Sun.
The spacecraft carries four main instrument suites to study magnetic fields, plasma, and particles.

disputed: Minor discrepancies in exact closest approach distance numbers (such as 3.83 million miles versus 3.9 million miles or 4 million miles) should be generalized or attributed as approximations in the script.
